Job-market sweep for Prabhavit Gupta, a Venice-based AI/automation engineer. Today is 5 August 2026. Three sweeps have already run. Your differentiator is **freshness**: find postings published in the last 7 to 10 days that the earlier sweeps could not have seen, across every host and title.

## Candidate profile (never invent beyond this)
- ~3 years experience across eight European companies. **Indian passport, Italian EU long-term residence permit** -> no sponsorship needed anywhere in the EU. NOT UK, Swiss or US authorised.
- Venice-based. **Confirmed open to: remote from Venice, remote-within-Germany, an office in any EU city, and Spain.** Do not down-score EU relocation.
- Stack: n8n (deep), TypeScript/JavaScript, Next.js, React, Node, PHP/Laravel, Supabase/PostgreSQL, Playwright, Claude Code, OpenAI + Anthropic APIs, Eden AI, Make.com/Zapier/Tray.ai, RAG, LLM agents with human-in-the-loop, Docker, AWS basics. Certifications: Microsoft Copilot Studio, Microsoft AI agents, Power Automate, Tray.ai Build Practitioner.
- Flagship: FlowSpace (Mar 2024 to ongoing) - grew platform 2,000 to 4,500+ users, led Bubble.io to Next.js + Laravel migration on a live product, built AI support agents, CRM lead capture and enrichment, GTM/outbound automations, scraping/parsing pipeline. Integrations: Office RnD, Nexudus, Clubee, Sendgrid, Google APIs. Also Urlink (built a platform largely with AI as PM and developer), UltraStrategy (CV-parsing tool in n8n + Eden AI), Clubee (API integration, unit testing, QA).
- **No GitHub. No CS degree.** No Java, no Go/Rust, no Python backend depth, no Kubernetes, no ML research, no Vue, no WordPress. English only, Italian beginner and studying.
- Salary target EUR 30,000-40,000. Contract EUR 200/day. **Sole trader on an Italian Partita IVA, NOT a limited company** - clients requiring an LTD/SRL are dead ends.

## Method: newest-first
Titles are wide open - anything a mid-level engineer with that profile could do. What matters is that the posting is NEW.

Use the search surfaces that actually expose dates and sort by recency:
- `jobs.workable.com/search/<country>/remote-<keyword>-jobs` - renders in a browser with reliable "Posted N days ago" labels. Try country slugs italy, spain, germany, netherlands, portugal, ireland, poland and keywords automation, integration, ai, full-stack, typescript, engineer.
- `arbeitnow.com` search and its english-speaking-jobs feed - BUT its dates are scrape dates, not liveness, so corroborate on the employer's own board before reporting.
- `euremotejobs.com` region and tag feeds (its listings carry a real posted date and the eligibility sentence).
- `himalayas.app`, `remotive.com`, `jobicy.com`, `nodesk.co`, `weworkremotely.com`, `remoteok.com`, `wellfound.com`.
- Ashby and Greenhouse org posting APIs where you can guess a slug: `api.ashbyhq.com/posting-api/job-board/<org>` exposes `publishedAt`, and `boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/<org>/jobs?content=true` exposes `updated_at`. Use these to FIND recent things, then verify separately.

Report anything scoring 55+ regardless of title, as long as you can show it is recent and live.

## Verification is the whole job - read this twice
Fetch-based verification has failed repeatedly in this project:
- **Ashby posting pages are client-rendered and a DELETED Ashby URL still serves its old page title.** Four of the highest-scoring finds in an earlier sweep were reported live by `api.ashbyhq.com` and returned "Job not found" the second a real browser opened them. A title match proves nothing.
- **Greenhouse board APIs report closed jobs as live**; fetching the posting URL then serves the multi-job board index instead of a posting. Confirmed twice.
So for every row: fetch the posting URL, require BODY content (a location line plus requirements plus ideally an application form), and **state your confidence explicitly with what you actually saw**. Mark anything you could not read as unverified rather than scoring it as live.

## Exclusion list - already applied to, closed, gated or logged. NEVER report these again:
Arize AI, Arkipel, Attio, Avatria, TransPerfect, Ben, Bullpen Talent, Camunda, Catawiki, Celonis, Checkly, Clera, Codex, Cognite, Cohere, Contentful, Cosuno, Cresta, Dash0, Dataiku, Docplanner, MioDottore, DADA ENERGY, Dust, Duvo, Eight Sleep, EggAI, ElevenLabs, Eneba, epilot, Facile.it, Filigran, Fueled, G2i, Glacis AI, Goldsky, Goodweek, GRAI, GTM Base, Gensyn, HiPeople, Implement Consulting Group, Integral, Jamie, Jimdo, JobLeads, Kairos, KFS GROUP, Langdock, Laioutr, leadtech, Lia, Loomya, Lovable, MailerLite, MAIA, Make, Mavriq, Mercura, Mindrift, Toloka AI, Moneyfarm, Musixmatch, MyEdSpace, Novosafe, Nuitee, Oh, OpenHands, Parloa, peopleIX, Pinnipedia, Pragmatike, Quadrivia, Reedsy, Reflow, Remote People, Resend, Reverse, RevOS, Runpod, salesHAX, SalesCaptain, Satispay, Shippeo, SIXT, Sourcegraph, Starbridge, Stackgini, supermodular.ai, Supabase, Sysdig, Taxfix, TEVEO, tem, The Flex, The Global Talent Co, Twilio, Unframe, Vercel, Viktor, YLD, ZOE, Zapier, alago, cargovibe, dexter health, n8n, neptune.ai, Nearform, Aircall, Always Friday, Outliant, ClickHouse, Neural Earth, Atmen, GitLab, Hightouch, Firecrawl, Encord, Ophelos, Nooks, Exa, Roger, Jobgether, Customs Support Group, Aivisory, Platform Venture Studio, Sword Health, Empatica, NFON, MLabs, Storyblok, Typeform, Intercom, Constructor, Certivity, Ludicrum Tech, Plain Concepts, ALEA, AppXite, Quadcode, Everseen, Check Point, Vyntra, Tomra, Candescent, Del Oro Consulting, Appfire, Supaapps, Scalia, Tech Holding, Tempo, IntervAI, IESF, Metrikflow, Sokra, Clera-AI, Lionhires, Obvious, Hypha, Decentriq, Umana, Philogen, Enginium, AiWonder.

## Scoring (total 100)
role match 30 + eligibility and work basis 25 + stack overlap 20 + seniority realism 15 + signal quality 10. Kill most of the 25 for UK/Swiss/US authorisation requirements or a non-EU office. Do NOT penalise EU relocation. Penalise talent marketplaces with no named end client.

## Output - return this and nothing else
One block per role scoring 55+:

### <score> - <role title> · <company>
- **Where:** <verbatim location/eligibility sentence> · Tier 1 (Venice today) / 2 (EU but a move) / 3 (outside the EU or authorisation he lacks) · Employee or Contract
- **Language:** <verbatim language requirement, or "none stated">
- **Pay:** <figures or "not disclosed"> · **Posted:** <date, and how you know it>
- **Why:** two or three sentences tied to specific things he has actually done.
- **Watch-outs:** the honest gaps, named.
- **Apply:** <canonical application URL>
- **Verified:** <what you fetched, what you saw, your confidence>

Then a short "dead or unverifiable" list and the queries you ran. No preamble.

{"method":"project_read","path":"claude/application-rules.md","content":"# Standing rules for submitting applications on Prabhavit's behalf

These are his instructions, not suggestions, and several of them exist because they were got
wrong once already. Read this file before touching a single form. If a rule here conflicts with
your own judgement about what would "look better" to an employer, the rule wins — it's his
career and his call.

## The non-negotiables

1. **Attach the CV to every application. Never submit one without it.** Use only the CV file he
   most recently supplied — the exact PDF, unmodified. Do not regenerate it, reformat it, or
   substitute a version you made. If the file isn't available in this session, stop and ask;
   don't proceed with a CV-less application.

2. **Salary or rate expectation: €30,000–40,000.** Write it plainly — "€30,000–40,000" or
   "EUR 30,000–40,000, negotiable" at most. **Do not** pad it with explanations about market
   bands, do not substitute a higher figure because the posting advertises more, and do not
   write a paragraph where a number was asked for. If you think his number is low, say so once
   in chat and then use his number anyway.

3. **Never leave a cover letter field blank when one is asked for.** Adapt his motivation letter
   (`assets/motivation-letter.md`) to the specific role. Where the form takes a file, generate a
   PDF; where it takes text, paste the adapted body.

4. **When a form asks for years of experience and wants 3 or more, write 3.** Don't skip an
   application because a year count is above his. Answer honestly with 3 and let the employer
   decide. Same principle for any "do you have N years of X" free-text field: give the true
   number and one clause of context, no more.

5. **Skip join.com** unless he has signed in on that browser. Their apply flow forces account
   creation or Google sign-in, and account creation is off-limits.

6. **Don't make the writing sound AI-generated.** Details in the writing section below.

## His details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | Prabhavit Gupta (preferred: Prabhavit) |
| Email | prabhavitg@gmail.com |
| Phone | +39 351 610 7807 (country: Italy, +39) |
| Address | Via Zanetti, 10 · Venice · Veneto · 30175 · Italy |
| Location for city pickers | Venice, Venezia, Italy |
| LinkedIn | https://www.linkedin.com/in/prabhavit/ |
| GitHub / portfolio | none supplied — leave blank rather than inventing one |
| Work authorisation | Italian EU long-term residence permit. **Needs no sponsorship anywhere in the EU.** Not UK, Swiss or US authorisation. |
| Availability | Immediately — the FlowSpace contract ended July 2026 |
| Languages | English professional, Hindi native, Italian beginner |

Standard answers to the questions that recur:

- *Legally eligible to work where you'll work from?* → **Yes**
- *Which status allows you to work there?* → **citizen / permanent resident** (the EU long-term permit)
- *Will you require sponsorship now or in future?* → **No** for EU-based and remote-from-Italy roles. For a **UK, Swiss or US** role, the honest answer is **Yes** — answer it truthfully and flag the role to him rather than fudging it.
- *Able and willing to work remotely?* → **Yes**
- *Based in Europe?* → **Yes**
- *Previously worked in a customer-facing capacity?* → **Yes** (FlowSpace: mediated between the internal team, an external agency and members; Urlink: project manager on client requirements)
- *Production experience at a large enterprise (1,000+)?* → **"only shipped in smaller companies or startups"** — true, don't inflate it
- *AI agents / agentic workflows?* → **"built and operated agentic systems in production, including testing for non-determinism and failure recovery"** — true, and his strongest answer on any form
- *BPMN specifically?* → he has n8n workflow automation in production but no BPMN. Pick the middle option where one exists; never claim BPMN production experience
- *Native English speaker?* → **No, fluent at C2 level**
- *Pronouns, gender, ethnicity, disability, veteran status* → leave blank or "prefer not to say". Never guess demographic data.
- *How did you hear about us?* → the honest answer is a job board; pick "Job Board" / "Other" and say "job board" if a follow-up field appears.

## Writing that doesn't read as machine-written

His own motivation letter is the voice to match: direct, concrete, slightly formal, first person,
specific numbers, no salesmanship. Things to avoid because they are the tells:

- Openings like "I'm excited to apply" or "I am thrilled by the opportunity".
- Three-item lists everywhere, and sentences of identical length stacked together.
- "Leverage", "passionate about", "cutting-edge", "seamlessly", "robust solutions", "I thrive in".
- Restating the job description back at them instead of saying what he did.
- Perfect symmetry. Real writing has a short sentence after a long one, and occasionally starts with "But" or "So".

What to do instead: name the specific thing he built, the tool he built it in, and the number it
moved. Say plainly where he's weaker rather than papering over it — a sentence like "my agent work
has been in n8n rather than a Python harness, so I'd be learning your idioms early on" reads as
human and costs nothing.

## The facts worth reaching for

Use these rather than adjectives. They're all on his CV.

- FlowSpace: took over an existing system, grew the platform **2,000 → 4,500+ users**, led the migration from **Bubble.io to Next.js + Laravel** on a live product, built the support **AI agents**, lead capture and enrichment into the CRM, GTM and outbound automations, and a scraping/parsing tool that increased listings.
- Integrations shipped: **Office RnD, Nexudus** (automated bookings), Clubee API, Sendgrid, Google APIs, OpenAI/Anthropic, Eden AI.
- UltraStrategy: **CV-parsing tool in n8n + Eden AI**. Get2Germany: Google API tracking, AI tools for finding courses and jobs. Clubee: API integration, unit testing and QA.
- Urlink: built a platform largely with AI, acting as PM and developer.
- Eight European companies in about three years (UK, Spain, France, Italy, Germany, Luxembourg, Netherlands) — the ramp-fast argument.
- Certifications: Microsoft Copilot Studio Agent Academy, Microsoft AI agents, Power Automate, Tray.ai Build Practitioner.
- Degree: BA Philosophy, International Studies & Economics, Ca' Foscari Venice. No CS degree — don't hide it, don't apologise for it.

## Things you must not do

- Create an account, set a password, or sign in as him.
- Solve a CAPTCHA.
- Enter payment details, government ID numbers, or a date of birth he hasn't given.
- Invent a GitHub link, a portfolio URL, a referral name, or demographic data.
- Claim experience he can't evidence — specifically BPMN, Python backend depth, ML research, or a language beyond English.
- Submit two applications to the same company for roles he clearly doesn't qualify for. One good application beats two scattershot ones.

When you hit one of these, stop that application, leave the form filled if you can, and tell him
exactly what's needed.

## Log every submission

After each one, record: company, role, the ATS, what was entered in each non-obvious field, the
confirmation text you actually saw, and the link. If you didn't see a confirmation, it didn't
happen — say so. He is tracking this in a spreadsheet and a silent failure is worse than a
visible one.
